newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real ends hair lower as mini-band cut again.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real ends hair lower as mini-band cut again.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.1 percent to close at 1.0346 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank surprised the market by setting a weaker mini-band just one day after the last drop, dealers said.
The Central Bank set the new trading band for the real by buying dollars at 1.0345 reais and selling at 1.0395 reais in a morning auction.
"Nobody was expecting a new drop in the mini-band this week," one trader said.
The previous mini-band was set Wednesday between 1.0335 and 1.0385 reais to the dollar.
Dealers saw the latest drop as a bid to aid exporters, concentrating mini-band reductions in the beginning of the month when exports usually are highest.
"The market did not think the Central Bank was signalling a change in the percentage it intends to drop the mini-band during the month," one dealer said.
So far this month, the mini-band has been lowered 0.2 percent. In the last few months, the mini-band was dropped between 0.5 and 0.6 percent.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real fell 0.11 percent to end at 1.0403 to the dollar, following the drop in the mini-band.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed at 1.098 per greenback, up 0.27 percent, traders said.
